cases.title: With the hand-placed switch on, a pipe text moved by hand onto a clash is left where it was put by Tidy labels (counted 'Placed by hand (left alone) 1') even when Tidy labels is told Yes
cases.plan_item: UX-LBL-01 hand-placed label stays, the Tidy labels half (daily card D13 profile B, switch ON)
cases.expected: With both switches on: the new pipe's start invert text IL 18.000 at P8 is moved by hand 5 mm down (it moves 5 mm); the SPOT LEVEL block 10EC5D is moved onto it as in R16; CDTIDYLABELS All then counts 'Placed by hand (left alone) 1', lists no 'start invert text would move' line, and after the Yes answer that text is still exactly where the hand put it (0 mm, within 0.5); the drawing holds the same number of objects.
cases.why_not_unit: The hand-placed mark is written by a real AutoCAD MOVE and read by a later live tidy in the real drawing.
not_automated: Card D13 step 3 (move pit P8 500 mm, the label must stay) is NOT driven: in the installed source only the Tidy labels pass reads the hand-placed mark (HandPlacedLabelRule is used only in LinkService.TextClashTidyUp.cs), so whether a pit move keeps a hand-placed label is a question for the desk and the card, not a check to guess.
The card names 'the pipe label'; this case moves the start invert text because it is the text with a proven clash (R16). The rule marks any pipe text moved on its own.
Profile A (switch off) is the twin N27_BROKEN.
